description: A place to meet up with friends, and also access useful services including Worcestershire Libraries, is located in Welland Village Hall. Serving people in Welland and the surrounding villages including the Hanleys, "Books & a Brew!" is Welland's Social Space and Library. It offers a lovely space to meet up with friends for a coffee, and also to access important services without having to travel to Malvern or Upton. On offer all year round is a "Help yourself" table of free hot & cold drinks & biscuits, free high speed wifi, popular free "Magazine Swap" table, kids colouring activities, lego and board games, and access to most of Worcestershire library's services (you can even return books that you have borrowed from any of the other libraries in Worcestershire). In addition, through the year, there is a programme of special events, including activities and competitions for children, and also valuable opportunities to access useful services right here within the village, such as those provided by Citizen's Advice, Age UK and West Mercia Police. Information about these will be available on the Parish Council website's News page and its Facebook site as well as on posters on the village hall and village notice board next to the shop. All are welcome at Books & a Brew! - you don't have to be a member of Worcestershire Libraries to come along. Dogs on leads also welcome. Open weekly M 2.30-4.30pm, W 8.30-12.30pm, Th 10am-12pm & monthly 10am-12pm on 3rd Sat. Closed Bank Hols & Christmas week. Worcs library services available, also hot & cold drinks, cake/biscuits, kids colouring activities, & free magazine swap table.

description: Day Centre – Warm Space Availability - Available to Health and Social Care Staff only. Note: Please be aware, this warm space facility may close without prior notice. We recommend calling ahead and making an appointment before planning your visit each time. Our Day Centre is open Monday to Friday during daytime hours, with a limited number of spaces available. Last year, in addition to day centre facility we introduced this warm space specifically for health and social care workers who spend time working outdoors in low temperatures and need a warm place to take a break. Staff may be waiting outside clients’ properties according to their rota and, when temperatures are particularly low, can use this space to rest and stay warm. To access the facility, uniform and valid ID are required. The company reserves the right of admission in line with infection prevention and control procedures. Facilities include Wi-Fi, disabled toilets, mobile phone charging points, tea/coffee with snacks, books, sensory room, prayer room and arts crafts. Staff can also join in any activities taking place while they are in the warm space. Please note that we regularly take photos and CCTV records enjoyable moments within the facility; by using the space, you consent to these recordings and potential publication of the data. For more information, please call the telephone number provided. During extreme cold weather, we may be able to extend the opening hours and days of the warm space facility. Currently we are not affiliated with any of charities. We operate independently and are only offering the warm space facility to support health and social care staff. We also work under the guidance of Leicester City and County Council Homecare Social Services Department regularly. Health and Social Care Staff - let us make this place a success by availing the warm space during the winter months. If you are a registered Charity with surplus resources and would like us to extend these services to wider population, please call us to discuss further. Thank you. Carers Direct Homecare 01162736066

description: You will find Baillieston Care Home located on the outskirts of Glasgow. We are a short distance from local shops, round the corner from the nearest bus stop and stone’s throw away from Glasgow city centre, making us easily accessible for visitors to pop-in for a chat. Our team is committed to enriching the lives of each of our residents. Our team offers nursing care for those who have complex medical needs, as well as nursing dementia care provided by specialist teams trained in the complexities of looking after those living with dementia, who may also have other long-term medical conditions. description: pop in for a coffee and a chat Everyone needs social connections to survive and thrive. But as people age, they often find themselves spending more time alone. Being alone may leave older adults more vulnerable to loneliness and social isolation, which can affect their health and well-being. Studies show that loneliness and social isolation are associated with higher risks for health problems such as heart disease, depression, and cognitive decline. If you are in poor health, you may be more likely to be socially isolated or lonely. If you are socially isolated or feeling lonely, it can put your physical and mental health at risk. Adults who are lonely or socially isolated are less healthy, have longer hospital stays, are readmitted to the hospital more often, and are more likely to die earlier than those with meaningful and supportive social connections.

description: We run a Community Hub every week on Tuesday mornings (we began in November 2022). We offer a welcoming space for people to meet and have hot drinks and something light to eat. We also provide papers, magazines and puzzles. We provide tea, coffee and cake ‘on a pay as you feel’ donation basis (with free tea and coffee refills). Some people like to pop in for buttered crumpets or teacakes; our ‘bacon butties’ mornings are always popular. We often have themed days, e.g., Pancake Day, where we served fresh pancakes, and also had fun events (including pancake races for children). We also have craft activities (e.g., mosaic making sets), that visitors can come and sit and do, as we have found these mindful activities help people relax, and provide a focus for people who are struggling with anxiety and mental issues. Tables are also set up in the small side room (off the main hall) to provide a ‘quiet space’ for those who find social settings difficult, and this also serves as a ‘shared working from home’ space. Free Wi-Fi is provided. We have incorporated a Parent & Toddler group into the Community Hub, which has been well used and goes from strength to strength. During the holidays we have encouraged the attendance of older siblings and provided craft activities for them to do. We are keen to promote sustainability in the community whenever we can – the GRowsley community group and local allotment holders donate excess produce. Visitors are encouraged to help themselves to these local vegetables, fruit and jam or chutney, or to exchange items e.g., blackberries and apples when in season.

description: Pan Together is an Island charity which exists to support and provide a community hub for the residents of East Newport, which includes the Isle of Wight's most disadvantaged area. Our purpose-built centre comprises: a community cafe providing wholesome, affordable food whilst also acting as a social hub; an IT learning suite; two community rooms; a large training kitchen; and an outside produce-growing area. We provide: vital signposting and support for people needing help and advice; we help to avert social isolation; there are free courses in Maths, English and IT; free weekly drop-in sessions for people wanting to brush up their skills and/or get help with their CV and/or are thinking about returning to work after a break; volunteering and work experience opportunities; social activities such as bingo; cookery sessions for children and vulnerable families; and a new money management advice and form-filling service to support people in these tough economic times. We run a community larder twice a week for local residents. Members pay £5 per weekly visit for two carrier bags of fresh, frozen, refrigerated, tinned and dried food and other household essentials which they choose for themselves. If they pick wisely, they'll receive £20 to £30 of goods and no one needs a referral.

address: Draper Hall, London, London SE1 6TL
description: At Draper Together, our aim is to build a stronger, more connected community by providing activities and services that address social isolation, food insecurity, and youth development. Rooted in the heart of Southwark, we focus particularly on supporting vulnerable residents in and around Elephant and Castle. We run a wide range of activities that cater to the diverse needs of our community. Our weekly Kids' Club offers a safe, nurturing environment where young people can engage in creative learning and build friendships. We operate a twice-weekly food bank and a weekly food hub, providing essential support to families facing hardship. For older residents, we host regular social activities designed to combat loneliness and encourage community participation. In addition, we facilitate a weekly men's wellness group at Clapham Cube, combining boxing and mental health discussions to promote emotional resilience and personal growth. Draper Together is a registered charity, governed by a Board of Trustees who bring expertise in community development, education, health, and the arts. Our day-to-day operations are overseen by a small, dedicated team of staff and volunteers, led by myself as Director. We are deeply embedded in the community we serve, and our approach is always collaborative and responsive to local needs. Decision-making at Draper Together is democratic and community-driven. Major strategic decisions are made by the Board of Trustees, informed by regular consultation with staff, volunteers, service users, and local partners. We actively seek feedback through surveys, community meetings, and informal conversations, ensuring our services remain relevant and impactful. Our management style is hands-on, flexible, and rooted in a genuine commitment to empowering the community. Ultimately, Draper Together exists to create a welcoming, supportive space where people of all ages and backgrounds can thrive. We believe in the power of local action to transform lives, and every activity we deliver is a step toward a stronger, more resilient community.

description: SPACE OPENING ON 1st October 2026** Elderberries Vintage Tea Rooms is a friendly and inclusive community space supporting people in later life across Bexley. We provide a warm welcome, affordable hot meals and refreshments, companionship, social activities, practical information and opportunities to build meaningful connections. Many of our guests are living alone, experiencing loneliness or isolation, coping with bereavement, managing health conditions, caring for someone else, or finding it difficult to access information and services. Our staff and volunteers take time to listen, build trusted relationships and help people feel valued, connected and more confident. We also provide informal support with digital exclusion, including help to understand online safety, scam awareness and how to access useful NHS information. Visitors can receive information and signposting about carers’ support, local services, health and wellbeing, and other sources of practical help. Our team includes trained Dementia Friends, and we aim to provide an understanding and supportive environment for people living with dementia and those who care for them. We encourage preventative care by sharing accessible advice and helping people find support before problems become more serious. Where someone needs additional help, we can connect them with other Evergreen Care services or trusted local organisations. Elderberries is free to enter, with meals and refreshments available at affordable prices. No referral is required. People in later life, carers, family members and members of the wider community are warmly welcomed.

address: All Saints CHURCH EXMOUTH, Devon EX8 1RZ
description: Three years ago Stephen moved from Plymouth to Exmouth and saw a call out in the local paper for someone to run the local stroke survivors’ club. He applied and got the role. ‍ Stephen is a Christian and says he tries to support others from all different backgrounds “because I’ve been there himself”. I don’t ask what he means by that, but he does later say he’s had several strokes and TIAs. ‍ Initially, the group met in Exmouth Pavillion; then they used a council building. More recently, they’ve been using All Saints’ Church in Exmouth. The church hall is open two days a week until 3pm as a Warm Welcome Space. (Stephen calls it a Warm Hub.) Exmouth Stroke Survivors' Club space visitor ‍ “We felt sometimes people wanted it for longer so now people can come back from 6pm or 7pm. We have some entertainment. We’ve had Elvis nights and all sorts,” says Stephen. ‍ “We get food donated from Tesco and Marks & Spencer each week which we use for meals,” says Stephen. Other food donations go to people in the community who can use it. Volunteers at the Exmouth Stroke Survivors' Club ‍ On a Monday and a Wednesday, the Stroke Survivors’ Club gives a dinner, “at dinnertime”. The Club also delivers food parcels to people who can’t come to the meetings for whatever reason, charging a nominal £3 for delivery (waived for those who really can’t pay). ‍ Sometimes, club members check on others and offer advice, for instance on energy saving and payments. “People say thank you, if it wasn’t for you I wouldn’t know what to do,” says Stephen, unassumingly. ‍ Funding has been an issue, but the Survivors’ Club charges a yearly subscription and they have held several fundraising events including a quiz and a gardening activity for which they were donated plants and soil. Sport England even gave them a table tennis table. ‍ And that’s not it: the Club teaches cookery skills to people on low incomes or those who’ve had strokes, showing them how to use vegetables and what they might have in the kitchen cupboard. ‍ “I want to make sure people feel looked after,” says Stephen. Mothers' Day montage ‍ The Club has grown from five or six people three years ago, to 75 club members today. It really is the most fantastic example of a space serving its community –
title: Exmouth stroke survivors club community

description: Fallowfield Secret Garden is a volunteer-led, urban Permaculture project which aims to develop a beautiful, biodiverse green space for the local community to meet, eat, learn and play. The project was set up in 2011 and has gone from strength to strength through the support of local volunteers and neighbours. Our 1.5-acre site, hidden away in the middle of a housing estate, has been transformed from an overgrown wasteland to a thriving community space which now includes a vegetable garden, kid’s forest play area, orchard, wildlife pond, medicinal garden and a wooden roundhouse. The garden is run by a core group of 10-15 volunteers who give their time each week to make sure it is open for anyone to join, whether volunteer or just to visit. We are open all year round for at least 3 days per week. Members of the core group divide the responsibilities for leading different projects onsite, running activities/events with overarching responsibilities including communications and volunteer coordination. We are a constituted community group with a Board comprising a Chair, Secretary and Treasurer. Decisions are made by consensus in meetings, or decision-making can be devolved to working groups with specific responsibilities and roles.

address: Bangladesh Welfare Association, Hyde, Cheshire SK14 1LF
description: Hyde Bangladesh Welfare Association (HBWA) was formed in 1976 by a group of local Bangladeshi people. The community centre is based in Hyde (Tameside) in the Werneth Ward, which is located next to the Godley ward (according to 2001 Census is one of the most deprived wards of the country). Both these wards house most of the 10000 Bangladeshi community of Tameside. Early indication from the latest census shows the demographic and status is much the same, with increase in population and higher unemployment issues. HBWAs objectives are: To represent the needs of local Hyde community in accessing local services. To promote capacity building and community cohesion by organising social and cultural events which Create a better understanding between the diverse communities. To provide additional support to Bangladeshi people in Hyde with cultural and language Barriers in accessing services. To provide advice and guidance on issues for the community in welfare, housing, health, Education, employment and immigration and other areas. To provide training opportunities for local people to improve the employment and education levels and improve the quality of life. HBWA was set up originally by people originating from Bangladesh. Bearing this in mind, our organisation celebrates memorable days of Bangladesh which include: Independence Day, Victory Day, Mother Tongue Day and religious Eid celebrations annually, along with other annual celebrations like International Women’s Week and volunteers Week. We also deliver regular training, courses and workshops in the year to enhance the knowledge skills and experiences of local people, which helps their personal development. We work in partnership with other agencies in the area and the local authority to offer the best services to the community with lots of choices, options and awareness of what is available to them. The projects and services we run here are on a needs basis for the community after regular consultation and feedback for what the local people want.

description: Imagine Louth is a community-focused play centre and cosy café in Louth, Lincolnshire, run as a Community Interest Company (CIC). Its goal is to support wellbeing, connection and inclusion for families, children, and older residents. The café offers a relaxed, family-friendly space with barista coffees, teas, homemade soups, salads, toasties, treats and kids’ meals. Parents and carers can enjoy food and drink while children play and learn through imaginative role-play areas designed for ages roughly 6 months to 10–12 years. Alongside the café and play space, Imagine Louth runs workshops, craft sessions, home-education activities, wellbeing groups, birthday parties and community events for both children and adults. It also provides subsidised access where possible to ensure no one is excluded due to circumstances. A key part of its mission supports older and vulnerable residents through affordable, freshly cooked meals delivered to their door, helping those who may struggle to cook, live alone, or lack access to healthy home-prepared food. As a CIC, Imagine Louth reinvests its income back into the community, creating a welcoming hub that brings people together, reduces isolation, and offers play, nourishment and support across generations.

address: Letchworth Garden City Heritage Foundation, Letchworth Garden City, Hertfordshire SG6 3BF
description: Museum at One Garden City is a vibrant micro-museum in Letchworth inviting visitors to discover the story of the world’s first Garden City. Beautifully designed, welcoming and interactive, the museum’s photographs, iconic objects and rotating décor, take audiences on a memorable journey through the commercial, educational, and domestic history of Letchworth Garden City. Learn how Letchworth’s founder, Ebenezer Howard, combined the best of both town and country to make the Garden City a great place to live and work. Admire the 60s retro sideboard and telephone table, and immerse yourself in the style of a mid-century home furnished by Meredew of Letchworth, one of the most important contemporary furniture manufacturers in the UK. Other design success stories that you can admire include the Chater-Lea bicycles and the Everyman’s Library, created by publisher J. M. Dent who built Temple Press in Letchworth to print the one shilling, which are now collectable classics. Offering something for everyone, young children can play at a full-size shop with counter and original working till. A smaller market stall entertains the younger shoppers with aromatic carbolic soap and pear drops evoking days gone by. Grab a pen and leave your mark on the museum’s whiteboard wall! Exhibits are updated regularly with historical objects from the Garden City Collection: an archive of over 250,000 objects looked after by the Heritage Foundation. The museum is located at One Garden City, off Broadway Gardens, and open every Monday to Saturday from 10am to 4pm.
title: Museum at One Garden City

address: Newcastle Cathedral, Newcastle upon Tyne, Tyne and Wear NE1 1PF
description: Newcastle Cathedral has been a beacon of light for the people of the North East for nearly 800 years. For much of that time, our iconic Lantern Tower has served as a sign to our communities that they were approaching safety and belonging as they returned home to this city and region. Inspired by Jesus Christ, the Light of the World, the Cathedral today continues to serve its communities through its deep commitment to being a place of radical welcome, offering inspiring worship, and striving to empower worth within all who come into contact with us. Whilst we are based in the City of Newcastle, we are also the ‘Mother Church’ of the Diocese of Newcastle, and seat of the Bishop of Newcastle. Newcastle is the Church of England’s most northerly diocese, covering the whole of Northumberland as well as areas covered by Newcastle City and North Tyneside Councils. Our role is to be a focus of unity and a resource for the Church of England’s 240 local churches and 49 schools, which are also striving to be beacons of light where they are located.

description: The Orchard Trust’s Stowfield site, set in the Forest of Dean, offers a unique, inclusive environment for adults with learning disabilities through a Day Service, Therapy Suite, and a community-accessible Smallholding. Everyone is welcome to come to our site. We have a number of different care homes across the Forest of Dean. Our Stowfield site is home to a smallholding including animals and horticulture, along with fully trained staff, changing places, accessible paths and a warm community room where we run regular events. Our smallholding can be accessed by the local community, our clients and any visitors. It offers an activity park, an encounter barn, a rabbitarium, a sensory garden, therapeutic animals interactions, a productive allotment, an orchard, a covered outdoor space to rest, and various activity areas. We regularly run coffee mornings, film nights and larger festivals on our site for clients and the wider community. In addition to our dedicated staff, a number of local volunteers help us to maintain and develop the site. We also offer a variety of our site facilities for external hire, including Therapy Suite, the Day Service’s canteen area, the sensory room, a kiln, the outdoor site, fields and workshop.

description: Our warm space is a welcoming haven where everyone in the community can come to relax, enjoy a hot drink, and connect with others. It’s more than just a place to stay warm; it’s a safe, friendly environment where people can share stories, build relationships, and find comfort in a sense of belonging. We understand the importance of creating spaces that bring people together, especially during challenging times, and our warm space is here to provide support, kindness, and a little brightness to anyone who needs it. Alongside a warm welcome, visitors can take part in our popular Knit and Natter group, enjoy a friendly game of bingo, or spend time in our Camerados Public Living Room, a space designed to encourage conversation and companionship. Located next door to the Book Cycle, the warm space also provides the perfect opportunity to browse for a book and enjoy some quiet time with a hot drink. We have also partnered with Girls Club, who host regular coffee mornings, helping to create a varied programme of activities that appeals to a wide range of people. Our warm space has welcomed 1,142 people, becoming a valued local resource for those looking for company, support, or simply a comfortable place to spend time. Visitors benefit from opportunities to socialise, try new activities, and access informal peer support in a relaxed setting. Whether attending a coffee morning, joining a group activity, or enjoying a moment of peace with a book, people are able to take time for their wellbeing while feeling part of the wider community. This growing response demonstrates the ongoing need for inclusive spaces where everyone feels welcome and supported.

address: Restorative Justice For All International Institute, london, London SE16 2LJ
description: The RJ4All Rotherhithe Community Centre is South East London's hub of community empowerment and cohesion. Through the Centre, we aim to implement our Founder's vision of making SE16 London's first restorative post-code. At RJ4All, we believe that in order to achieve community cohesion and reduce anti-social behaviour, first we must adopt a holistic approach that addresses the reasons that lead to divisions. Poverty and power abuse must be rooted out, if we are genuinely interested in supporting and empowering communities to participate and indeed enjoy civic life equally. To this end, all local service providers (public, private and voluntary) must come together and under the guidance of the restorative justice values of power sharing, equality, dignity and respect support local communities. With the above vision in mind and with the support of our landlord, Clarion Futures Communities , Southwark Council and many local stakeholders, we have set up the following services, which are open to anyone: community fridge, education and digital inclusion, social community space, health and community cohesion, youth club+, wellbeing circle cafe, charity shop and safe house.

description: Soham Community Wellbeing Space is based at Savoy Court Community Centre in North Harrow. It is operated by Soham Community CIC, a not-for-profit organisation using accessible movement, mindfulness and healthy-living activity to improve wellbeing and social connection. Our Warm Welcome offer is free to enter and provides a heated, friendly and non-judgmental place where residents can sit, share tea or coffee, meet others and take part at their own pace. Activities include gentle chair-based movement, simple breathing and relaxation, mindfulness, healthy-living conversations and informal signposting to local support. The venue has a kitchen, seating, toilets including an accessible toilet, and space for both group activity and quieter participation. We welcome the general public, with particular attention to older adults, people with limited mobility or long-term health conditions, people experiencing stress or loneliness, carers, families, children and SEND families. No previous yoga or fitness experience is needed. Activities can be adapted using chairs, walls and props, and participation is always by choice. Although Soham Community CIC is at an early stage, the delivery team has several years of experience running yoga, meditation, chair yoga, children's wellbeing, community events and free or donation-supported sessions in Harrow. We are now bringing this experience together into a clearer year-round community wellbeing space. Volunteers help with welcoming, registration, refreshments, set-up and participant support. We use safeguarding, risk assessment, consent and referral procedures, and aim to build stronger links with local voluntary organisations, community venues and health and social-prescribing partners.

description: The Strand Centre is a community centre on the main high street in Dawlish, run by the Strand Community Trust. The centre comprises the Inspire Café, a large Auditorium, and several smaller rooms. We are a registered Place of Welcome within the community. The centre is a warm space for people to find respite and quiet, as well as to engage with others in the community. There are a series of programmed events, including groups such as a weekly Age Concern UK lunch club, the Men’s Shed, toddler groups, and a group for those with special educational needs. A street chapel is available for those who wish to engage in quiet reflection away from the main centre activities. The manager and volunteers are sensitive to the diverse needs of centre users, and will talk especially with those who are alone to see if they require specific provision or just some friendly conversation and a listening ear. Centre users can stay as long as they like throughout the opening hours with no pressure to purchase food or drinks. Homeless individuals use the centre to obtain respite, receive free refreshments, and receive clothing, bedding and food parcels. description: SPACE OPENING ON 17th October 2026** For the past six years, the Silver Age Project has proudly delivered a Warm Welcome Space in partnership with Harrow Council, providing a safe, welcoming, and inclusive hub for older people. Our aim is to reduce isolation, create meaningful relationships, and foster a strong sense of belonging within the local community. Our Warm Welcome Space is open weekly throughout the colder months, offering a warm, comfortable environment where older adults, particularly those on low incomes or struggling to heat their homes, can spend time, socialise, and take part in a range of free activities. These include gentle physical exercise sessions, educational workshops on topics such as energy-saving tips and healthy eating, digital skills training to help people stay connected, and fun group quizzes that encourage friendship and wellbeing. Over the past six years, we have supported more than 1,000 older adults, many from underserved communities, including people living with disabilities or long-term health conditions. We work closely with Harrow Council to distribute warm packs during the winter and provide complimentary hot drinks and biscuits at every session, ensuring everyone feels welcome and cared for. In addition to offering a warm space, we provide practical support by helping older residents access cheaper energy tariffs, apply for assistance from energy suppliers, and connect with local authority support schemes. Our Warm Welcome Space is much more than a heated venue—it is a trusted community hub that helps older people stay warm, improve their wellbeing, build lasting friendships, and access the support they need to live independently.

description: Swansea MAD is a grassroots, anti-poverty, anti-racist, pro-equality, pro-environmental, inclusive youth and community charity. We work for a fair world in which people can be themselves and thrive! Swansea MAD develops inclusive safe spaces for people to access advocacy, creative arts, education, digital access, employability support, training, campaigning activities and projects to bring fairness and belonging and to influence change for the better. Swansea MAD is part of the Swansea Spaces scheme as a local drop-in Warm Welcome hub, supporting and welcoming people to free food, hot drinks, toiletries, period products, charging points, SIM cards, digital devices and data (and training and support on how to use them). We also provide information and support about energy tariffs and efficiency and support people to register for the Priority Services Register. Swansea MAD also hosts food event every month, where everyone is welcome to share a hot meal and have a chat. Connect with us on our social media platforms to know the dates.

address: 216 High Street, Swansea, West Glamorgan SA1 1PE
description: Our Warm Welcome Space is a vibrant community hub where people come in from the cold – practically and emotionally – and leave feeling warmer, calmer and more connected. It is free, inclusive and non‑judgemental, open to anyone who needs a safe place to be, whether they are facing the cost of living crisis, digital exclusion, loneliness or all three at once. The atmosphere is intentionally homely rather than clinical: there is always a hot drink, a friendly greeting and someone ready to sit down and listen without rushing. Guests can simply rest and chat, or they can take part in activities, get practical advice, and build skills. A distinctive feature of our space is our integrated digital support offer – people bring in phones, laptops and letters they are worried about, and receive patient, one‑to‑one help to access essential online services, benefits, health, housing, work and learning. Over time, our space has become a trusted anchor in the community. People are referred to us by local agencies when digital barriers, money worries or isolation are blocking progress, because they know they will be met with warmth, dignity and expert support. Many guests go on to volunteer, help others with digital tasks, or contribute to running activities, so the hub is powered by the same people it supports. Our Warm Welcome Space is not just somewhere to keep warm; it is a place where people rediscover confidence, friendship and a sense of belonging.
title: Swansea MAD Warm Welcome Hub

description: 💙 The Braintree Hub The Braintree Hub is a community-focused centre in Braintree, Essex, operating as part of the wider work of the The Witham Hub charity. It exists to support local residents by providing practical help, affordable food, and a welcoming space to connect. 🌱 What the Braintree Hub is: A community hub and support centre A trading arm of The Witham Hub charity A place designed to bring people together and reduce social isolation Its core aim is to create a more connected, inclusive community, where everyone feels they belong. 💛 What it offers The Braintree Hub provides a mix of essential support and community services, including: 🛒 Community Supermarket Affordable groceries and household items £5 annual membership Prices significantly lower than typical supermarkets Helps individuals and families manage the cost of living 🤝 Support & Advice Guidance and signposting to services Help for those facing financial hardship or difficult circumstances 🧠 Social & Community Support A safe, welcoming environment to meet others Opportunities to share experiences and reduce loneliness Activities and spaces that encourage connection and wellbeing 🏡 A place for everyone One of the key principles of the Braintree Hub is that: It is open to everyone, not just those on benefits It removes stigma by offering support in a dignified, inclusive way It provides an alternative to crisis support like foodbanks by offering a more sustainable, everyday solution. 🌍 The bigger picture The Braintree Hub works alongside the Witham Hub to: Tackle poverty and social isolation Provide accessible community services Strengthen local support networks Together, they create a joined-up approach to supporting communities across Essex. ✨ In simple terms The Braintree Hub is a welcoming, practical support centre where people can access affordable food, find help and advice, and feel part of a supportive community

description: We offer a weekly programme of inclusive, community-focused activities designed to support wellbeing, reduce isolation, and foster connection. Our space is open and welcoming, with someone on-site most weekdays from 9am to 3pm, ensuring visitors can always drop in for a chat, a cuppa, or simply a place to rest. Monday – (our main Welcome space day!) Welcome Space & Chair-Based Exercise From 10am, we invite people in for tea, biscuits, and friendly conversation. At 11:15am, Alison leads a gentle chair-based exercise class suitable for all abilities. At 12pm, we serve a hearty hot meal with dessert, followed by more tea and coffee. The session typically winds down by 2pm, but the space remains accessible from 9am to 3pm. Tuesday – Community Café Our café runs from 10:30am to 12:30pm, offering affordable refreshments and a relaxed social atmosphere. Anyone experiencing hardship is discreetly offered free tea or coffee. The venue is staffed from 9am to 3pm, so visitors are welcome to pop in at any time. Wednesday – Open Drop-In & Bingo From 10am to 4pm, the space is open for anyone seeking warmth, company, or a quiet moment. We also host a friendly bingo session, open to all, which brings laughter and light-hearted competition. Thursday – Quiet Access Day While no formal activities are scheduled, the centre is staffed from 9am to 3pm. Visitors are welcome to drop in for a chat, a drink, or simply to enjoy the warm, safe environment. Friday – Activity Hub Running from 10am to 12pm, this free session encourages gentle physical activity and social interaction. We offer games such as indoor curling, darts, cards, and Scrabble. Bacon or sausage cobs are available to purchase, and tea and coffee are served throughout. The centre remains open from 9am to 3pm for anyone needing support or company. Weekends – Community Events & Private Hire Saturdays and Sundays are typically reserved for private bookings, but when community events are scheduled, we warmly welcome all attendees.

description: TogetherWORKS is a community-driven hub and not-for-profit Community Interest Charity (CIC), established in partnership with South East Wales Energy and opened in September 2021. We exist to strengthen our community by providing a welcoming, inclusive and accessible space shaped directly by local need. Our activities and groups are designed to reduce isolation and loneliness, improve wellbeing, and create opportunities for people to come together, share skills, exchange knowledge, and build confidence. A key part of our work is supporting people to relieve poverty and reduce financial pressures, including practical energy advice and support. We help individuals and households to better understand and manage their energy use and access the support they are entitled to. We also recognise and respond to food poverty within our communities, signposting and connecting people to food support through our Corner Cupboard, as well as providing access to essential personal hygiene items and pet food for those in need. Everything we offer is free or pay what you can, ensuring that cost is never a barrier and that all services remain accessible to everyone in the community. In addition, we host regular drop-in sessions with partner organisations, ensuring that residents can easily access advice, services, and support in a relaxed and trusted community setting. Every week, TogetherWORKS opens its doors to hundreds of local people seeking friendship, support, learning opportunities and a sense of belonging. From Welsh conversation sessions and Spanish classes to knitting groups, book clubs, yoga, breastfeeding support, men's breakfasts, disability support groups and LGBTQ+ peer support, our hub brings together people who may otherwise remain isolated within their own communities.
title: TogetherWORKS Caldicot

Market Hall, Chesterfield Sharlaine Fincham sharlainefincham@cfcct.org.uk We are proposing for the Youth Hub to provide a warm, engaging space to accommodate young people in the community. We are open for drop-in sessions for young people to come in to talk, share their concerns, play games, have fun, charge their phone, use WiFi and have the opportunity to be listened to. We would use this opportunity to consult with the young people further to establish what they would like in this space and how they would like it to be used. We would like to be able to provide a more welcoming environment for young people – bean bags/soft furnishing, etc. We already have some board games, an X-box and craft activities. We would also like to be able to provide hot drinks, snacks and food, which would be provided through the air fryer and induction hob, ensuring that all young people would be able to have something hot to eat or drink. We would work with other local organisations and providers to be able to offer sanitary products and food. The Youth Hub is also a base of support information offering sign posting to all services that support young people. description: Warmth and Wealth: Digital and Financial Empowerment" is an ongoing project providing a safe and supportive environment for individuals to build digital and financial confidence. Hosted weekly on Thursdays at the Community Action Centre in Evelyn Ward, the initiative helps participants navigate welfare applications, budgeting, and essential online services while fostering community connections. The Community Action Centre is open Monday to Friday from 9 AM to 5 PM, ensuring a welcoming space for those in need. The project features weekly digital literacy sessions, financial inclusion workshops, and peer support groups, designed to help individuals gain practical skills and access housing, employment, and healthcare services. We also provide access incentives such as Wi-Fi vouchers, travel support, and digital tools to remove barriers to participation. Through these sessions, we aim to create an inclusive, empowering space where individuals feel supported in developing independence and resilience.
title: Warmth and Wealth

address: 14 New King Street, Deptford SE8 3HS
description: Creating Space' is designed to empower individuals—particularly those experiencing homelessness, financial hardship, and social isolation—by providing essential skills for greater independence and wellbeing. Through structured activities such as cookery classes, financial literacy workshops, and peer mentorship, participants will gain practical knowledge to manage their daily lives more effectively. Additionally, a warm and comfortable environment will be available for individuals facing fuel poverty, ensuring they can access hot drinks, support services, and social engagement opportunities. The programme includes wellbeing sessions covering stress management, confidence building, and holistic self-care, alongside financial inclusion sessions that offer guidance on budgeting, debt management, and accessing benefits. Cookery sessions will promote healthy eating on a budget, reducing food waste, and strengthening food security. By fostering social connections, reducing isolation, and equipping participants with the necessary tools for self-sufficiency, 'Creating Space' aims to create lasting positive impacts within the community.

description: Luton Libraries are open to the public to join and make use of our building resources. This includes books, PC’s, photocopying and more. We also host regular activities across all our branches for all ages and abilities to join in with. Specific activities taking place in the library, together with any charges as necessary, are listed below. On Mondays from 10:30am to 11:15am a session entitled Mindful Stretch, for which participants are required to pay £3 each session. On Mondays from 4pm to 4:45pm Library Games for children aged 8 years and above. On Tuesdays from 10am to 10:30am Rhyme Time for pre school age children. On Tuesdays from 4:30pm to 5pm Real Play for children aged between 5 and 7 years. On Thursdays from 10am to 10:30am Rhyme Time for pre school age children. On the first Thursday of each month a Reading Group for adults takes place starting at 2pm. On Fridays from 10:30am to 11:15am a session entitled Mindful Yoga, for which participants are required to pay £3 each session. On Fridays from 1pm to 2pm Creative Arts, this is for adults only and participants are required to book in advance. On Saturdays (in term time only) from 11am to 12 noon Code Club for children aged between 8 and 12 years. On Sundays from 11:30am to 12 noon Rhyme Time for pre school age children. Please note that warm drinks/refreshments are not provided by libraries. Members of the public are welcome to bring in their own tea/coffee flasks etc. from elsewhere though. Libraries are open to all during opening hours. Certain activities are age restricted, please speak to a team member for more information. Full details can be found on our website: https://www.lutonlibraries.co.uk/home

description: @Flo's - The Place in the Park. Pay-As-You-Can on Mondays From 12-2pm on Mondays our normal menu is suspended and instead we will be serving a delicious hot lunch, sweet treat and hot and cold drinks on a “pay what you can basis”. There is no judgement and how much you pay is anonymous- everyone is welcome! The café is open the rest of the time from 10am until 4pm serving delicious brunch, hot lunch specials, sandwiches, salads, and sweets, expertly roasted coffee. All the money spent at the café feeds into the local economy and funds our community activities at Flo’s. Pay-as-you-can Mondays are part of the OX4 Food Crew- a partnership of local organisations working to tackle food inequality in OX4.

description: Over the colder winter months, we understand that many people face fuel poverty and struggle to afford heating costs. This is why we have funded a number of Warm hubs that can support people during the cost-of-living crisis. Warm hubs provide a safe place which is warm, friendly and welcoming where attendees can partake in social activities surrounded by the company of others whilst receiving support during difficult times. They offer a lifeline for people in social isolation and those suffering with fuel poverty. Places for People have funded warm hubs across three Places Leisure centres in Sheffield, where the pubic can enjoy a warm and welcoming space. The centres will be open from December until March, giving locals a chance to meet new people, play board games, and join in other activities. They will also offer free blankets and refreshments, with visitors to Wisewood and Graves given free hot food and drinks at selected sessions, while visitors to Thorncliffe will receive hot drinks and snacks. Opening Times Locations Wisewood Sports Centre: 75 Laird Rd, Sheffield S6 4BS Graves Health & Sports Centre: Bochum Pkwy, Jordanthorpe, Sheffield S8 8JR Thorncliffe Health & Leisure Centre: Pack Horse Ln, High Green, Sheffield S35 3HY More information Warm Hubs | Places Leisure – Places Leisure

hours._text: Places Leisure Warm Hub opening times vary; Wisewood is open to all from 1-3pm on Mondays and 9.30-11.30am on Fridays. Graves will be open from 1-3pm every Tuesday, Saturday and Sunday, while Thorncliffe opens 1-3pm on Wednesdays and 9.30-11.30am on Thursdays. The initiative will run through to March 2023.

description: The Millennium Gallery brings the best in art and design to Sheffield The gallery's changing exhibition programme showcases the best in national and international art and design alongside the region's remarkable creative talents. You'll also find collection displays celebrating Sheffield's metalworking prowess and the remarkable art and artefacts brought to the city by the artist and writer, John Ruskin. Sheffield's Metalwork Collection is one of the finest in the world. You'll see over 800 examples of the cutlery, flatware and tableware that have made the city famous, as well as beautiful objects collected from every continent. The gallery is also home to the Guild of St George's unique Ruskin Collection. Spanning art, illustrated manuscripts and minerals, the collection was established in the 1800s to inspire the people of Sheffield. Today, it's showcased through regularly changing displays celebrating the contemporary relevance of Ruskin's visionary ideas. There's also a cafe, Ambulo, on site which is open Tuesday-Sunday.

description: Weston Park Museum tells the stories of Sheffield and its people, from pre-history to present day. You can enjoy a warm welcome and explore free exhibitions and displays, alongside a programme of talks, tours and events. Originally opened in 1875, Weston Park Museum has found lifelong fans in younger visitors and grown-ups alike for nearly 150 years. You'll discover everything from archaeological treasures to zoological wonders, meet visitor favourites Spike the Woolly Rhino and Snowy the Polar Bear, and find out more about the people and events that shaped the city we know today. It's also home to a programme of changing exhibitions and events for all ages. In the Picturing Sheffield gallery, you'll see Sheffield-themed highlights from the city's art collection, including work by Pete McKee, Jo Peel, Stanley Royle, Joe Scarborough, and Emilie Taylor, as well as John Singer Sargent's much-loved The Misses Vickers. You can explore life in Ancient Egypt and unearth amazing artefacts spanning centuries in the Beneath Your Feet gallery. Over in What On Earth, you'll find out more about the city's changing wildlife and environment. In Sheffield Stories and Sheffield Life & Times, you'll discover the people and events that shaped the city and how life in Sheffield has changed over the years. There's also a cafe, Ambulo, on site which is open Tuesday-Sunday.

description:
Cadog's Corner is a welcoming community hub based in East Barry, providing affordable food, wellbeing activities, support services, and opportunities for people of all ages to connect and thrive. Our aim is to tackle food poverty, reduce social isolation, improve wellbeing, and strengthen community resilience through a range of inclusive services and activities.
Our services include community cafés, a low-cost community shop, wellbeing support, family activities, training opportunities, support groups, and community events. We work closely with local partners to ensure residents can access the support, information, and opportunities they need. The Memory Café offers a free, safe and fun place for members of the local community who are living with Memory Loss. Carers and family members are welcome to attend.
The Café is run by volunteers and offers free refreshments along with activities designed to enhance physical and mental well-being, e.g. Quizzes’, Crafting,Singalongs, light exercises, and team games. The Café also boasts a Community Liaison Officer and resource table to provide support on any queries café visitors may have e.g. Welfare Rights, carer support, local services etc.The Memory Café will provide a hot meal, and on-site support for our visitors.
